column1: # Hand written command -> package claims. Wins over anything tools/mine-cs.sh
# scrapes, and is where a claim goes that the scrape cannot make.
# Two kinds of entry belong here.
#   Commands defined with \def or \protected\def, which mine-cs.sh does not
#   read, because reading \def as well drags in a thousand package internals.
#   \includegraphics, \toprule and \mathbb are all in this group and are all
#   among the commands authors most often forget to load a package for.
#   Commands more than one package declares, where the scrape cannot say which
#   one an author meant. \square and \lozenge are both amssymb and marvosym;
#   amssymb is the answer in every document that is not about symbol fonts.
# Every claim here is checked by tools/verify-hints.sh, which compiles a
# document with the package and one without it. A command the kernel already
# provides fails that check and must not be listed.
# --- graphics: \def forms the scrape cannot see
# --- amsmath environments and operators reached through \def
# --- disputed between amssymb and a symbol font package; amssymb is meant
# --- siunitx v3 spellings, which the v2 compatibility layer also declares
# --- hyperref, defined with \def behind option processing
# --- cleveref, worth naming because \cref is easily mistaken for a kernel form
# --- bibliography, where the two families disagree and the log names which
# --- tikz / pgf, where the package name is not the file the author loads
